AppVersion.description:
A published version of an app, addressed by the digest of its bundle.

The row is written `pending` before the artifact is stored and marked
`ready` after — see the migration for why that ordering is the one that
makes a crash mid-publish visible instead of leaving an orphan artifact.

app_id.description: The app it is a version of.

created_at.description: When the version was first published.

digest.description:
The bundle's content address: `blake3:` and 64 lowercase hex characters.
The same bytes always have the same digest, which is what makes
publishing idempotent.

state.description:
`pending` while the artifact is being stored, `ready` once it is. A
successful publish always returns `ready`.

CertState.description: The three certificate states a person is told about.

CertificateStatus.description:
Where an org's wildcard certificate stands, in the words a person sees.

The same field on the org-creation response and the publish response.

message.description: What it means for reaching the org's apps.

Claim.description: What a claimant must publish to prove control of a domain.

auto_join.description:
Whether people whose Google hosted domain is this domain will join the
org automatically. Off unless asked for.

expires_at.description: After this the claim cannot be verified; start a new one.

id.description: The claim's id, for the verify call.

slug.description: The slug the org will get on verification.

txt_name.description: The TXT record name to create.

txt_value.description: The TXT record value to publish.

auto_join.description:
Whether people signing in with a Google Workspace account in this domain
join the org automatically. Defaults to off; only the person who verifies
the domain can change it later.

domain.description:
The domain to claim: the hosted domain of the Google Workspace account
making the request.

slug.description:
The new org's slug, `{app}.{slug}.clwd.run`. Permanent: it can never be
changed or reused. May not start with `p-`.

CreatedOrg.description: A newly created domain org and its certificate's state.

auto_join.description: Whether people whose hosted domain is this domain join automatically.

DomainSetting.description: The result of changing an org domain's auto-join flag.

Envelope.description: Every 4xx and 5xx response carries this body. Branch on `code`; `message` is for people.

message.description: A human-readable account of this occurrence.

request_id.description: Correlates this response with server logs. Also sent as `x-request-id`.

retryable.description: Whether the same request, unchanged, could succeed later.

IssueRequest.description: A request to issue a token.

app_id.description:
Narrow the token to one app in the org. A token bound to an app can only
issue tokens bound to that same app.

name.description: A label for the people deciding which token to revoke: 1 to 100 characters.

scopes.description:
The scopes to grant: any of `read`, `write`, `publish`, `admin`. Each
must be held by the token making the request.

IssueResponse.description: A newly issued token. `token` appears here and nowhere else, ever.

app_id.description: The one app it is bound to, or `null` for the whole org.

id.description: The token's id, for revoking it.

name.description: The label it was issued with.

token.description:
The token itself. Shown once: only its digest is stored, so it cannot be
recovered. The only time this value leaves the process.

PublishResponse.description:
The publish response: the version, and where the org's certificate stands.

`certificate` is here because the first publish is when an org's apps first
need to be reachable: a personal org gets no certificate until then, so its
first publish is also the start of the window in which `{app}.{org}` fails
the TLS handshake. The same field, with the same wording, as org creation.

bearerAuth.description:
A token looks like `clwd_tok_` followed by 64 lowercase hex characters, and is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Each operation names the one scope its token must carry; scopes are independent, so `admin` does not imply `publish`.

Tokens are issued by `POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/tokens`, which itself needs an `admin` token. Until sign-in exists, an org's first token is created by an operator with database access (`control-plane bootstrap-token`): there is no way to obtain a first token through this API.

sessionCookie.description: **Authentication:** a browser session cookie, set by Google sign-in (`GET /auth/google`). A state-changing request must also come from the control plane's own origin: `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`, or, without that header, an exact `Origin` match. Other pages on the same site, including every app under the apex, are refused.
sessionCookie.name: __Host-clwd_session

info.description:
The control plane API. Every operation lists the scope it needs and every error it can return, with what each error means and what to do about it.

## Authentication

A token looks like `clwd_tok_` followed by 64 lowercase hex characters, and is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Each operation names the one scope its token must carry; scopes are independent, so `admin` does not imply `publish`.

Tokens are issued by `POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/tokens`, which itself needs an `admin` token. Until sign-in exists, an org's first token is created by an operator with database access (`control-plane bootstrap-token`): there is no way to obtain a first token through this API.

## Errors

Every 4xx and 5xx response carries the `Envelope` body. Branch on `code`, which is stable; `retryable` says whether the same request could succeed later.

| Code | Status | Retryable | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `control-plane.invalid_request` | 400 | no | A request body or parameter was not acceptable. The message says which part and why. | check the request against the OpenAPI schema at /openapi.json |
| `control-plane.payload_too_large` | 413 | no | The request body is larger than this endpoint accepts. The message states the limit. | reduce the upload below the stated limit |
| `control-plane.method_not_allowed` | 405 | no | The path exists, but not for this HTTP method. | use one of the methods named in the Allow header |
| `identity.unauthenticated` | 401 | no | The request carries no valid credential: the Authorization header is missing or malformed, or the token is unknown or revoked. These are deliberately indistinguishable. | supply a valid, unrevoked API token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |
| `identity.forbidden` | 403 | no | The caller is authenticated but not permitted to do this: a token without the scope the operation requires, a signed-in user who is not the one allowed to make this change, or a browser request from another origin. The message says which. | act on what the message names: a token with that scope, the permitted user, or a request from the control plane's own pages |
| `control-plane.not_found` | 404 | no | The resource does not exist, or it is outside what this token can reach — another org, or another app when the token is bound to one. These are deliberately indistinguishable. | check the identifier, and that the token's org, and its app if it is bound to one, cover this resource |
| `control-plane.conflict` | 409 | no | The request conflicts with the resource's current state. | re-read the resource and retry with the current state |
| `control-plane.artifact_corrupt` | 500 | no | A stored artifact could not be decoded. This is a server-side integrity failure, not a problem with the request. | this is a server-side integrity failure; the artifact must be rebuilt and republished |
| `control-plane.timeout` | 504 | yes | The request exceeded its time budget, or a dependency did not answer in time. | retry; if it persists the dependency is down rather than slow |
| `control-plane.rate_limited` | 429 | yes | This token has used its request budget. The message and the Retry-After header say how long to wait. | retry after the number of seconds in the Retry-After header |
| `control-plane.internal` | 500 | no | An unexpected failure inside the service. | this is a defect; report it with the request id |
| `bundle.*` | 400 | per code | The uploaded bundle was rejected by the bundle format. The code, `bundle.*`, names the specific defect. | See the bundle format's code table: https://github.com/clwdrun/clwd/blob/main/docs/error-codes.md |

No operation produces `control-plane.artifact_corrupt` today; they are listed so the catalogue is complete.

get.description:
Google redirects here with `code` and `state`. Validates the flow cookie and `state`, exchanges the code under PKCE, verifies the ID token, finds the user by Google subject, and issues a fresh session cookie. Every rejection — a missing or tampered flow cookie, a mismatched `state`, a refused or replayed code, a failed ID token — is the same `identity.unauthenticated`.

**Authentication:** none.

post.description:
Uploads a bundle and records it as a version of the app, addressed by the digest of its contents.

Idempotent: publishing the same bytes again returns the existing version with 200 rather than creating a second, so a retry after a timeout or a dropped connection is always safe.

**Authentication:** a bearer token carrying the `publish` scope.

post.description:
Starts claiming a domain for a new org. The caller must be signed in with a Google Workspace account whose hosted domain is the domain claimed. The response names a TXT record to publish; verifying it creates the org. Nothing is reserved until then, and the claim expires after 72 hours. `gmail.com` and `googlemail.com` cannot be claimed.

**Authentication:** a browser session cookie, set by Google sign-in (`GET /auth/google`). A state-changing request must also come from the control plane's own origin: `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`, or, without that header, an exact `Origin` match. Other pages on the same site, including every app under the apex, are refused.

post.description:
Checks the claim's TXT record and, if it carries the claim's value, creates the org with the claimed slug, binds the domain to it and makes the caller a member. The org's certificate is issued afterwards, asynchronously: the response's `certificate` says where that stands. A domain already verified by an org is never moved.

**Authentication:** a browser session cookie, set by Google sign-in (`GET /auth/google`). A state-changing request must also come from the control plane's own origin: `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`, or, without that header, an exact `Origin` match. patch.description:
Sets whether people signing in with a Google Workspace account in this verified domain join the org automatically. Only the person who verified the domain may change it.

**Authentication:** a browser session cookie, set by Google sign-in (`GET /auth/google`). A state-changing request must also come from the control plane's own origin: `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`, or, without that header, an exact `Origin` match. Other pages on the same site, including every app under the apex, are refused.

Issues an API token for the org. The response carries the token itself, once: only its digest is stored, so it cannot be shown again. Sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

A token can only issue a token no stronger than itself: every requested scope must be one it holds, and a token bound to an app can only issue tokens bound to that app.

**Authentication:** a bearer token carrying the `admin` scope.
